preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000) representing the number of words.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(l) <= 1000 for l in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: The second line contains N space-separated integers, each representing a word length (1 ≤ length ≤ 1000).
The input consists of exactly two lines: the first line with N, and the second line with N lengths.

postconditions.description: If no valid set of words exists, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by N words, each matching the corresponding input length.

postconditions.expression: all(len(word) == int(l) for word, l in zip(stdout.splitlines()[1:], stdin.split()[1:])) if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: Each output word must have the exact length specified in the input.

postconditions.expression: all(word in {'0', '1'} for word in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: Each word must consist only of the characters '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(not (word1 in {w[:len(word1)] for w in words} - {word1}) for word1 in words) if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else True
postconditions.description: No word is a prefix of another word, where words is the list of output words (excluding 'YES').
